title: The video bar's buttons say what they do, in the app's own voice
goal: The row of buttons over the trim strip is eight unlabelled glyphs, and hovering one gives a tooltip that looks like nothing else in the app. You cannot tell what any of them does without trying it. They should read the way every other control in Photonz reads, and say what they do in the same way.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-20 with a screenshot of the trim bar, hovering the scissors: "tooltips don't look like any other tooltip. I don't know what the buttons do." The tooltip in the shot reads 'Split at Playhead (B)' in a plain dark rounded box that is not the app's tooltip.

The app HAS a tooltip system and these buttons are not using it. Look at .toolTip(_:key:fallback:) which the tool bar uses (every tool shows a tooltip that names it and its key, a shipped task), and panelHelp which the panel uses. One of those is the right answer for this row; a third look is not.

The icons are the other half and are worth checking rather than assuming: eight glyphs in a row with no labels, several of which look like glyphs used for other things elsewhere in the app. There is a done task 'edit-is-one-glyph-across-the-corpus' about exactly this kind of drift, and an icon conformance epic. Check this row against the same rule.

This is a small task and it is deliberately narrow: it is about the row of buttons reading correctly, not about whether that row should exist. Where the video surface goes is the design pass's question and is blocked on a decision card.
acceptance: The tooltip on these buttons is the same tooltip the rest of the app uses, drawn the same way, with the same shape, type and timing, and the audit shows one of each side by side
Every button in that row says what it does and what key presses it, using the app's existing tooltip vocabulary rather than its own
The glyphs themselves are checked against the app's icon set: one that means something different elsewhere in the app, or nothing anywhere, is replaced, and the audit lists what each was and became
Somebody who has used the rest of the app can name what each button does from the row alone, checked with a person rather than asserted
The row is checked against the design language the mocks set for this surface, and where it diverges the audit says whether the mock or the app won and why
It reads correctly in light and dark, at every window size, and the buttons that cannot act right now are dimmed rather than silently doing nothing
Audit under queue/audits/ with the row captured and a tooltip beside the app's standard one, and anything rough filed as a follow-up
